standard.title: Write with unjoined letters
standard.description: write words using unjoined lower-case and upper-case letters
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have been developing foundational pencil grip and letter formation at Foundation level. They have not yet consolidated consistent, legible unjoined letter formation across both lower-case and upper-case letters in writing.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students write words using unjoined lower-case and upper-case letters.

nodes.label: Functional pencil grip
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can hold a pencil with a functional grip that allows sustained writing without fatigue or loss of control.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate a functional pencil grip that allows them to write at least a sentence.
nodes.typical_width: Hold a pencil with a consistent functional grip across writing tasks, sustaining control and comfort through short writing activities.
wider: Explore alternative writing tools (marker, chalk, stylus) and discuss how grip adjusts
Reflect on grip comfort during longer writing tasks and adjust when needed
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a functional grip, students cannot produce the controlled letter formation required for N2 and N3 — formation exercises collapse without physical control of the tool.

response_modes.reason: Pencil grip is a physical habit that requires repeated practice to consolidate. Regular writing activities build the muscle memory and automaticity needed for a functional, sustained grip.

success_criteria: Student holds the pencil with a functional grip (not fist grip) consistently
Student can write a sentence without loss of control

nodes.label: Consistent lower-case letter formation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can write all lower-case letters with consistent, recognisable formation.
nodes.minimum_width: Write all lower-case letters legibly with correct formation direction.
nodes.typical_width: Write lower-case letters with consistent size, orientation and formation direction, producing legible writing across words and sentences.
wider: Compare letter formation across different scripts or fonts — discuss what makes a letter recognisable despite variation
Identify and practise letters that are commonly confused or reversed (b/d, p/q)
nodes.hinge_reason: Lower-case letter formation errors — particularly reversals — cascade directly into spelling and reading tasks; students who write b/d or p/q interchangeably cannot reliably encode or decode CVC words.

response_modes.reason: Lower-case letter formation requires sustained practice — particularly reversal-prone letters (b/d, p/q). Regular writing across varied tasks builds the automaticity needed for fluent handwriting.

success_criteria: Student writes all lower-case letters legibly with correct formation direction
Student distinguishes commonly confused letter pairs (b/d, p/q) consistently

nodes.label: Upper-case letter formation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can write all upper-case letters correctly and use them appropriately (sentence starts, proper nouns).
nodes.minimum_width: Write upper-case letters for sentence beginnings and at least one proper noun.
nodes.typical_width: Write all upper-case letters with correct formation and apply them in the appropriate contexts — sentence beginnings and proper nouns — in continuous writing.
wider: Explore contexts where all-caps are used (headings, labels) and discuss the convention
Write a short text and identify all correct upper-case letter uses
success_criteria: Student writes upper-case letters legibly in sentence-start and proper noun positions
Student does not apply upper-case letters mid-sentence incorrectly
